subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding curating, portfolio, and exhibition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about curatorial theme, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of curatorial theme.
Check, revise, or improve work about curatorial theme using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about curatorial theme.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Project work on curatorial theme. Project: plan, select, sequence, document, test, and revise a sustained body of work through curatorial theme, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Use available definitions and examples, but keep intent and scored decisions your own.
primary_task: Target for this probe session: Activate prior knowledge about curatorial theme, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of curatorial theme. Check, revise, or improve work about curatorial theme using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about curatorial theme; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. 1. Diagnostic: Before instruction, make or analyse a brief first attempt involving curatorial theme. Keep it unchanged; record three concrete noticings and one question. 2. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different project question, items to develop or select, private presentation format, sequence, revision and next-step priorities choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about curatorial theme, and it belongs to "Curating, Portfolio, and Exhibition", which also covers separate topics such as selection and sequencing. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about curatorial theme; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.

Authored success criteria for curatorial theme: The learner completes the central task about curatorial theme., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Learner-owned choices during this diagnostic starting point: project question, items to develop or select, private presentation format, sequence, revision and next-step priorities.
deliverable: Diagnostic, Reflection, with the observable Arts evidence and learner-owned decisions identified in each block.
critique_criteria: The submission contains an unchanged baseline; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.

The learner locates relevant purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting curatorial theme.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce curatorial theme to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one purpose relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact purpose evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply curatorial theme under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on curatorial theme rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

arts_music_r1.prerequisite_summary: curation plus the ability to complete a short study, loop, observation, or plan without aiming for polish.

concept_registry.meaning: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one purpose relationship while working on curatorial theme.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Direct middle-school arts language with constraints, choices, and stopping points separated.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for curatorial theme is present, but the record does not yet locate purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
